headline: Recommended approval of the 2026-2027 One Year Action Plan for Community Development Block Grant, Home Investment Partnership, and Emergency Solutions Grant programs.
summary: Recommended approval of the 2026-2027 One Year Action Plan by a 3-0 vote. Recommended marking work completed on item 26-0821, which addresses underutilized space, also 3-0. Items 26-1033 and 26-0831 were kept in committee.
decisions: Accepted the minutes of the July 1, 2026 meeting, 3-0.
Placed item 26-0870 on file, because it was replaced by item 26-0688.
Recommended approval of the 2026-2027 One Year Action Plan (item 26-0688), 3-0.
Kept in committee the mayor's update on item 26-0825 about the ADA Coordinator vacancy (ID 26-1033).
Kept in committee Resolution 26-0831 on a list of community spaces available for public use.

Recommended marking Resolution 26-0821 work completed, 3-0. The resolution asked the administration to engage with Saint James Church leadership about partnership opportunities for underutilized space.

transcript:
## City of Somerville, Massachusetts City Council Housing, Community Development and Equity Committee Meeting Minutes

Wednesday, September 30, 2026

6:00 PM

This meeting was held via Zoom and in person in the Committee Room and was called to order by Chair Strezo at 6:04 pm and adjourned at 7:14 pm on a roll call vote of 3 in favor (Councilors Sait, Link, Strezo), 0 absent.

Others present: Miranda Rubin - Program Compliance Officer, Thomas Galligani - Executive Director of Strategy and Development Department, Brenna Broderick - Community Partnerships Liaison, Madalyn Letellier - Assistant City Clerk Legislative Services.

Roll Call

- Present: Ward Five City Councilor Naima Sait, City Councilor At
- Large Jon Link and City Councilor At Large Kristen Strezo

1. Committee

Approval of the Minutes of the Housing, Community Development and Minutes

Equity Committee Meeting of July 1, 2026.

(ID # 26-1211 )

- RESULT: ACCEPTED
- AYE:

- Ward Five City Councilor Sait, City Councilor At Large
- Link and City Councilor At Large Strezo

2. Mayor's Request Requesting approval of the 2026-2027 Housing and Urban Development

(ID # 26-0870 ) One Year Action Plan for the Community Development Block Grant, Home

Investment Partnership, and Emergency Solutions Grant Programs.

This item was replaced with item #26-0688.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE PLACED ON FILE AYE:

- Ward Five City Councilor Sait, City Councilor At Large
- Link and City Councilor At Large Strezo

3. Mayor's Request Requesting approval of the 2026-2027 Housing and Urban Development

(ID # 26-0688 ) One Year Action Plan for the Community Development Block Grant, Home

Investment Partnership, and Emergency Solutions Grant programs.

Miranda Rubin and Thomas Galliagani from Strategy and Development and spoke to the Annual Action Plan and presented on the priorities of the plan,

HCDE - 20260930 - Public Engagement Presentation (with 26-0688).

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE APPROVED AYE:

- Ward Five City Councilor Sait, City Councilor At Large
- Link and City Councilor At Large Strezo

4. Mayor's

Conveying an update regarding item #26-0825, a Resolution that the Communication Administration submit a written report to this Council regarding the timeline (ID # 26-1033 ) and process for staffing the Americans with Disabilities (ADA) Coordinator

role and update this Council on the plan to process ADA complaints and accessibility coordination when this position is vacant.

Councilor Strezo sponsored constituent Holly Simione to speak on behalf of the Somerville Commission for Persons with Disabilities as the Chair.

- Commissioner Simione provided commentary from the commission
- regarding the vacancy for the Americans with Disabilities (ADA)

Coordinator. Concerns about the job description and if the appropriate candidates would be attracted to the role and the gap in hiring while meeting the needs of the public were addressed. Commissioner Simione also spoke

to the desire for the commission to have access to the ADA complaint emails so they are able to respond appropriately. Councilor Strezo posed the questions of how recruitment efforts are going and what measures are being

- taken, to which follow up with Human Resources will be necessary.

RESULT: KEPT IN COMMITTEE

5. Resolution

By Councilor Hardt, Councilor Clingan and Councilor Strezo

(ID # 26-0831 ) That the Executive Director of the Office of Strategic Planning and Community Development develop and share with the public, a list of all the spaces that are available for community use, including and especially those that are part of private developments.

- Thomas Galligani, Executive Director of the Strategy and Development

Department, stated a team was hired in 2021 to look at where community spaces existed along with basic details about how the community can use

them and the appropriate contact information. Director stated there is funding available from the community preservation act (CPA) to assist

current and future spaces to fit the needs of the community. The committee recognized there are mandated community spaces throughout the city that

already exist. In response to Councilor Link about the realities of maintaining the list, Director Galligani shared the goal to keep the list up to date and there are more community spaces in planning. Councilor Strezo

expressed desire to keep this item in committee until a comprehensive list is shared and more information is included on how residents can sign up for

- the spaces.

RESULT: KEPT IN COMMITTEE

6. Resolution

By Councilor Mbah and Councilor Hardt

(ID # 26-0821 ) That the Administration, the Executive Director of the Office of Strategic

- Planning and Community Development, the Director of Health and Human

Services, and the Director of the Office of Housing Stability, engage with leadership of Saint James Church to explore opportunities for partnership

between the city and the church to activate underutilized space for community-serving purposes.

- Brenna Broderick, Community Partnerships Liaison, was present to speak
- about the attached community space that has gone mostly unused. Councilor

Hard, Councilor Mbah, and she went to visit and identified three different spaces with the capacity of 80, 50 and 15. The opportunity to use the space has been circulated to community groups who have expressed a need and coordination continues with other faith organizations. She highlighted the logistical struggles around security and accessibility compliance that still need to be addressed to make it a space to serve all. Questions were raised about utilizing the space as a Teen Center and Liaison Broderick discussed

the complications of utilizing the space. The committee discussed the recently displaced Alcoholics Anonymous (AA) meetings and while two

have been able to relocate one meets during Sunday service hours, so places of worship are not compatible.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE MARKED WORK

COMPLETED

AYE:

- Ward Five City Councilor Sait, City Councilor At Large
- Link and City Councilor At Large Strezo
